numbers.value: modern nuclear 1.12-1.22; Heysham 1.08, CANDU 1.08; coal, steam, geothermal 0.81-0.90; gas turbines 0.72, 0.77; Calder Hall 0.67

note: INCONCLUSIVE under Test Card T033 (approved ad04e5965 before the table was read). Real plants scatter on both sides of the Curzon-Ahlborn efficiency: modern nuclear plants exceed it by 12-22 percent, gas turbines and an early reactor fall 23-33 percent below; the median gap of 19 percent is neither close (<= 10) nor far (>= 25). The AI reading 'systems run at D13's ceiling' is neither confirmed nor removed; the D13 ceiling itself assumes symmetric linear contacts, which real plants need not have (Esposito et al. bound eta* between eta_C/2 and eta_C/(2 - eta_C)). The first run attempt stopped on a CSV parse error (commas in plant names) before any result; the names were quoted, numbers unchanged. L2 (confronted, outcome inconclusive) approved by the author.
